longForm.overview:
🔴 is the emoji of red coded circle-shape read — a clean circle-pulse shape, the red filled-in silhouette, and the universal 'red circle-shape' tag for stop-signal. Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded circle-shape read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded circle-shape read, 🔴 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate red coded circle-shape — a 'red 🔴' stop-signal marker or a 'circle-pulse pulse 🔴' alert-marker reveal. The red fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern stop-signal aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as red coded rather than literal circle-shape-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🔴 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate stop-signal energy. A partner sends it on a 'red 🔴' stop-signal marker. A friend sends it on a 'circle-pulse pulse 🔴' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'red coded 🔴' list thread. The red fill cue is what makes the emoji feel red coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'red coded circle-shape moment.'

What separates 🔴 from the rest of the shape family is the red register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'red coded circle-shape,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why 🔴 travels especially well on partner stop-signal markers, alert-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with red energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🔴 in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The red coded circle-shape cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid 🔴 in 'literal object' or finish-coded contexts where the red energy feels off. A 'red 🔴' message works for stop-signal marker; for finish-coded contexts use 🏁 or a sentence.

Skip 🔴 when you want to communicate a different color. The red coded register is too red-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
